isolate.narration: Add a filter on the decisive field to isolate the failing records.

demonstration.narration: Open Add filter, choose ${var.field}, keep the operator as ‘is’, and enter ${param.incident.finding}. This asks Kibana to retain only failing records with the decisive value for ${truth.finding}.
demonstration.reasoning: The scoped window still contains failures from other services and causes. A field-level filter is a visible, reusable way to remove that noise and test whether ${truth.finding} appears within ${truth.scope}.
demonstration.evidence: After the filter is applied, the result table should shrink to failures where ${var.field} equals ${param.incident.finding}. Those records are the scenario signal behind “${truth.conclusion}”, which we will corroborate at document level next.

hints: Identify the field that separates the abnormal records.
Use Add filter (field, operator, value) — filter for the decisive value, or filter it out with is not to drop noise; you can also filter from a row or a field's top values.
Filter ${var.field} for the decisive value; Show me can add the reference filter.
